paragraphs: The services shown above all name Telford as an area they cover. Telford & Wrekin Council runs its own fostering service, and our Telford and Wrekin page lists the services covering the wider borough, so if you live in the town it is worth reading both pages before deciding who to speak to.

The main difference between a council and an independent agency is who assesses, approves and supports you. Fostering with the council means caring for the borough's own children, with its social workers behind you. An agency carries out its own assessment and approval, gives you a supervising social worker of its own, and cares for children that councils, Telford & Wrekin among them, ask it to look after. Fees, training and out-of-hours help vary from one service to another, so ask each one what it pays and what support it gives.

Telford & Wrekin Council's placement sufficiency assessment, which informed its plans for 2024 to 2029, counted 438 children in its care in November 2023. On those figures, 144 were in the council's own foster placements, 107 in what the council calls private foster care, and 53 with relatives or friends in kinship care. The council recruited 85 and 75 foster carers in 2019/20 and 2020/21, and 50 over the following two years, and the assessment records that its use of independent agencies has stayed steady. It also points to a growing need for homes for older children, including young people aged 16 and over, which is worth raising with any service if you feel able to care for teenagers.

For more choice, the Shropshire page lists six services and the Wolverhampton page nine. Speak to two or three, ask how they match children with carers and how soon your assessment could start, and compare their answers before you apply.
